ideas: Better quality items last longer and cost less overall
Cheap items meet urgent needs immediately
Depends on how often you use it

phrases.meaning: over a long period of time
saving money that costs more later
made to stay in good condition

model: I think it's usually better to save for a better one. First, good-quality items are cheaper in the long run. There's a saying, buy cheap, buy twice, and I learned that the hard way. A few years ago I bought a cheap office chair online. It looked fine in the photos, but after six months the wheels broke and the seat started to fall apart. I replaced it with a proper chair, which cost three times as much, but it's still perfect now, so the cheap one was really a false economy. Another reason is that better products are often built to last and are safer. For example, I put money aside for two months to buy a good motorbike helmet, instead of a cheap one from the market, because I use it every day. That's real value for money. Of course, if you need something urgently, you sometimes have to make do with a cheaper option. But overall, for things you use often, saving up is the smarter choice.
